overview: Food service managers run restaurants, cafeterias and catering operations. They hire and schedule staff, order food and supplies, check quality and safety rules, handle money and deal with customer complaints. O*NET rates knowledge of customer service at 4.53 out of 5 for this job and administration at 4.07. Most learn on the job, and O*NET data shows a wide mix of education, from 30% with a high school diploma to 19% with an associate degree. The BLS May 2025 median is $69,390 across 238,430 jobs. Expect long hours on your feet and some conflict.
pay: Food service managers earn a median of $69,390, and the top 10% earn $107,640 or more. Washington has the highest state median at $95,190, 37% above the national figure, followed by Massachusetts and Hawaii. California has the most jobs, 33,180, at a median of $78,260.

faq.q: How much do food service managers make?
faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $69,390 a year. The middle half earn between $56,870 and $86,800. Washington, Massachusetts ($92,240) and Hawaii ($87,800) pay the most, while Arkansas ($55,120) and West Virginia ($54,800) have the lowest state medians. Bonuses are common.

faq.q: Do you need a degree to be a restaurant manager?
faq.a: Usually not. O*NET places the job in Job Zone 2. In O*NET data, 30% of food service managers have a high school diploma, 21% a certificate and 10% a bachelor's degree. Most rise from cooks or servers, and food safety certification is often required.

faq.q: Is restaurant management a hard job?
faq.a: It can be. In O*NET data the job ranks above 97% of U.S. jobs for leading others and above 91% for serving the public. You spend long hours on your feet, handle tight deadlines during rushes and settle conflicts with staff and customers.

faq.q: What can food service managers do next?
faq.a: The closest moves are Chefs and Head Cooks (88% match), food preparation supervisors (78%) and gambling services supervisors (75%), based on O*NET 31.0. Most of these pay less, so many managers move up to multi-unit or regional roles instead.
